title: Reactive reserve leasing failure causing sustained reserved-pool depletion during high-burst traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a high-traffic burst window on 2026-03-09 the dedicated autoscaler began leasing reserve slots but failed to reconcile released leases, which produced a sustained depletion of available reserved pool capacity for ~22 minutes. Several customers with burst-enabled reserved pools experienced degraded throughput and elevated latency; two enterprise customers opened priority escalations to Support. Root cause appears to be a race between the lease-release reconciliation job and the new reactive-leasing path introduced in release dedicated-autoscaler-2026.02 that assumed idempotent release markers.

Impact timeline: 2026-03-09 14:07 UTC - first symptoms (increased headroom alerts). 14:10-14:32 UTC - customers observed request queueing and elevated p50/p95 latency; autoscaler did not create extra instances because reserved pool ledger showed zero free slots. 14:32 UTC - manual mitigation applied (reconcile job forced, temporary burst limit relaxation for affected tenants). 14:45 UTC - normal headroom levels returned.

Immediate mitigation performed: (1) forced ledger reconciliation via admin command; (2) temporarily increased per-tenant soft-burst allowance for affected customers; (3) opened PagerDuty incident and pushed comms to Support + account teams; (4) rollback of reactive-leasing path was staged but not executed because reconciliation restored service quickly.

Current hypothesis: the reactive-leasing code path writes an in-memory lease token then asynchronously writes a release marker. Under high contention the release marker write failed to persist during a short datastore leader change; the reconciliation job uses a filter that ignored leases without release markers (optimizing for common-case), causing leaked allocations. The reconciler's compact window was too long (30m), allowing visible depletion. The bug is in the reconciliation filter and the assumption that release markers are always present quickly.

Proposed fixes: (A) Patch reconciler to treat expired leases as eligible for reclamation regardless of release-marker presence and reduce compact window from 30m to 2m; (B) Make reactive-leasing write release markers synchronously (or at least with an acknowledged write) before acknowledging lease success; (C) Add stronger telemetry for lease lifecycle (create/write_ack/release_ack) and an SLO alert when reconciler-detected leaks > 1% of pool capacity for > 2m.

Plan of attack: 1) Short-term hotfix: deploy reconciler change to treat expired leases as reclaimable and reduce compact window to 2m (can be enabled via feature flag). 2) Observability: add lease lifecycle events to headroom dashboards and an alert. 3) Medium-term: harden reactive-leasing to persist release markers before returning success or add a two-phase commit trace. 4) Long-term: add chaos tests around datastore leader change and a canary that simulates high-concurrency lease churn.

Acceptance criteria: hotfix reduces time-to-reclaim to < 2m in the staging replay; new telemetry surfaces leak events and triggers an alert; reactive-leasing change validated in canary with zero regression in throughput.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created issue after post-incident triage. Support reported two escalations (ACME Health and BrightBank) with correlating reserved-pool shortages. Captured initial logs and timeline.

2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Investigated autoscaler logs; found 'lease_without_release' entries correlated with datastore raft leader transitions at 14:09 UTC. Attached preliminary query to enumerate leaked leases: https://internal-grafana.redwood/d/leaks/lease-query (PR described below).

2026-03-11 - Priya Desai (SRE): Ran forced reconciliation in prod for the affected region; this recovered capacity for impacted tenants. Recommendation: reduce reconciler compact window and add immediate reclaim for expired leases.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Drafted hotfix branch that relaxes the filter and reduces compact window. Test plan executed in staging with synthetic churn; time-to-reclaim improved from median 14m to 18s. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/8421

2026-03-12 - Engineering lead (Tom Nguyen): Approved emergency deploy for the reconciler hotfix behind a feature flag. Deploy scheduled to region us-east-1 at 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC with mitigations to quickly rollback if headroom oscillation observed.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Hotfix deployed to us-east-1. Post-deploy: no further reports of reserved-pool depletion during simulated burst tests. Rolling to other regions over next 48h.
2026-03-12 - Customer Success (Lina Park): Notified ACME Health and BrightBank of the mitigations and that patch is rolling; asked for any residual performance observations.
